outline.h2: What Makes a Good Wedding Hashtag
outline.answers: Direct answer for 'how to make a hashtag for your wedding' (PAA in every city): short, unique to you and easy to spell. Then exactly 4 one sentence takeaways.
outline.notes: Must include: direct answer and 4 takeaways. No numbers on length unless sourced; say 'short' rather than a character count (the AI overview's character limit is not a source).

outline.h2: How to Make Your Own Wedding Hashtag
outline.answers: how to make a wedding hashtag; how to make a hashtag for a wedding; how to come up with a wedding hashtag; PAA 'How can I make my own hashtag?'. The 'generator' as a method.
h3: Start With Your Names, Surnames and Initials
Add Wordplay That Sounds Like You
outline.notes: Test step: search the tag on the platform to see if it is taken, read it aloud, check where names join for unintended words, capitalise each word for readability. Instagram help (read 2026-11-26) states numbers are allowed but spaces and special characters such as $ or % will not work; use only as stated. Commas in H3s are fine; no colons, dashes or hyphens.

outline.answers: wedding hashtag ideas; wedding hashtags; funny wedding hashtags; destination wedding hashtags. Every example built from placeholder names (for example Sam and Alex Rivera); no real couples' tags and no tags lifted from SERP pages or AI overviews.
outline.notes: Destination is the gap: the 'destination wedding hashtags' SERP has no page that owns it. Give the most depth here (place name, venue town, island, 'weekend in' patterns, welcome dinner and farewell lunch variants). Do not reuse example tags shown in the AI overviews.

outline.h2: Why a Generator Is Only a Starting Point
outline.answers: Primary keyword 'wedding hashtag generator' and PAA 'Can ChatGPT generate hashtags?'. Honest framing: tools and chat assistants can produce a long list fast, but the couple still has to choose, test and check it, so the method above is what matters.
outline.notes: No claims about any tool, and no Wonderland Studio AI or hashtag claim. No third party generator named or linked. Natural place for the related link to /expert-advice/chatgpt-vs-ai-wedding-planner with a neutral anchor about using ChatGPT for planning. Not in the brief sections: optional, keep it short (two short paragraphs) or fold into the method H2 intro if the planner prefers.

outline.h2: Where to Share Your Wedding Hashtag
outline.answers: Where to show the tag (welcome sign, table cards, wedding website, invitation or welcome note, photo booth template, MC reminder) and one tag per event versus one for the weekend. Also seen in the 'wedding hashtags' AI overview.
outline.notes: Links /expert-advice/wedding-website and /wonderland-studio ('our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs' only). The brief groups this H2 and the next under one H2 (Using Your Wedding Hashtag Well); either structure works, the planner decides.

outline.h2: Public Hashtags, Private Albums and Guest Privacy
outline.answers: Public tag versus private shared album, guests with private accounts, asking guests before posting, and asking parents before posting photos of children.
outline.notes: Instagram help (read 2026-11-26): if you have a public account and add hashtags, the post is visible on the hashtag page; posts from private profiles will not appear publicly on hashtag pages. eSafety and OAIC facts reused from content/posts/wedding-photo-app/03-source-pack.json (fact_01 to fact_14, fact_21 to fact_23). Link /wedding-tools/wedding-photo-app here.

outline.answers: Close with one Wedded Advisor line from brand-facts 'Claims we can make' (one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact) and the Concierge and magazine CTAs.
outline.notes: Heading wording is the writer's choice within the rules.
